meta.scope: Batch offline processing 1K-15K call transcripts/day (3K in / ~500 out, JSON-constrained) on on-demand L4 24GB, A100 80GB, RTX PRO 6000 96GB (Blackwell SM120), H100 80GB; fine-tuned LoRA-merged or adapter models.
meta.method: GitHub REST API (gh/WebFetch) for versions, dates, stars, licenses; vendor docs and model cards for features. Values marked UNKNOWN or UNVERIFIED were not confirmable. WebFetch summaries are model-condensed; treat quoted wording as paraphrase unless in quotes.
caveats: llama.cpp: GitHub 'latest release' endpoint returned v0.9.0 (2026-11-04) while the newest build tags are bNNNN (b12224 on 2026-11-09). Both tag schemes appear in the repo; Winder.ai (Sep 2026) used b11179.

Data-quality note: model-correction facts in the task prompt: Granite 4.2 is a DENSE transformer (3B/8B/30B), not hybrid Mamba (IBM docs, HF card). Gemma 4 12B exists as '12B Unified' (11.95B dense) per HF blog; vLLM recipes list E2B/E4B/12B/31B dense + 26B-A4B MoE.

engines.maintainers_activity: Very high; community + Red Hat/Neural Magic, UC Berkeley origin, PyTorch Foundation project (foundation status not verified this session).
engines.continuous_batching: Yes (PagedAttention, V1 scheduler, chunked prefill). Scales output tok/s with concurrency: H200 Llama3.1-8B at 64 users ~44x llama.cpp tok/s (Red Hat); H100 Qwen3.8-27B 8-bit 1,610 tok/s at 50 conc (Winder.ai).
engines.prefix_caching: Automatic prefix caching, enabled by default in V1 (vLLM blog 2025-01-27: <1% overhead at 0% hit rate). Hybrid Mamba/SSM models: prefix caching via --enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint (needs EAGLE/MTP; docs, stable). NOTE: one docs fetch summary claimed 'not default' - conflicts with V1 blog; verify with `vllm serve --help` on target version.
engines.structured_output: xgrammar, guidance (llguidance), outlines; default 'auto'; lm-format-enforcer deprecated in v0.33.0 (removal v0.35.0). Offline: SamplingParams(structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json=...)). JSON schema, regex, choice, grammar, structural_tag.
engines.quantization: FP8 (Ada/Hopper+ for W8A8; Marlin FP8 weight-only on Ampere), AWQ, GPTQ, Marlin, INT8 W8A8, GGUF (experimental-quality), NVFP4/MXFP4 (native on Blackwell; Marlin W4A16 fallback on Ampere/Hopper/SM120). SM120 NVFP4 MoE: forum report (2026-04-11) says Marlin W4A16 was the only reliable backend for one large MoE; native FP4 GEMM bug on SM120 in FlashInfer (issue 2577, Feb 2026). Re-test on your build.
engines.lora: Multi-LoRA (--enable-lora, --lora-modules, --max-loras, --max-lora-rank), dynamic load/unload endpoints (VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING; security warning), LoRAResolver plugins (S3/HF), MoE LoRA incl. mixed 2D/3D formats. Supported-models table marks LoRA yes for Gemma4, NemotronH, GraniteMoeHybrid, GptOss, Qwen3Next, Phi3.
engines.hardware: NVIDIA compute capability >= 7.5 (T4, A100, L4, H100, B200); RTX Blackwell SM120 support noted since ~v0.15 (secondary source premai.io); official docs mention CUDA 12.9 wheels, v0.33.0 dropped CUDA 12.9 wheels. Also AMD ROCm, Intel XPU, TPU, CPU.
engines.openai_api: Yes (chat, completions, responses, embeddings; Anthropic-style also not verified)
engines.offline_batch: Yes: `LLM` class (offline_inference, takes list of prompts, structured outputs per request) and `vllm run-batch -i in.jsonl -o out.jsonl` (OpenAI batch file format; --max-inflight default 2x max_num_seqs, min 1024; outputs in input order).
engines.cold_start: vLLM/SGLang start in under ~90 s for a 70B FP8 in Spheron test (secondary, 2026-03-23); model load + torch.compile + CUDA graph capture time model-dependent; UNKNOWN for each target model. Google Cloud Run: GPU instances with drivers pre-installed start in ~5 s (excludes model load).
engines.ops_ease: Docker image vllm/vllm-openai; pip/uv install; large flag surface; fast release cadence means pin versions; many recipes at docs.vllm.ai/projects/recipes.
engines.production_readiness: High; the de facto default for batch and multi-tenant serving; vendor model cards (Gemma 4, Nemotron 3.5, Granite 4.2, Qwen3.8, gpt-oss) list/recommend it first.
engines.security: No auth by default unless --api-key; runtime LoRA loading endpoint is a risk if exposed; no telemetry-by-default claim verified (usage stats collection exists, opt-out via VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS / DO_NOT_TRACK - from prior knowledge, UNVERIFIED this session).
vendor_recommended_by: Google Gemma 4 (model card lists vLLM first)
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning BF16 card (vLLM primary)

engines.maintainers_activity: Very high (LMSYS/RadixArk community; NVIDIA, AMD contributors). Pre-1.0 versioning - frequent breaking changes noted in release notes.
engines.continuous_batching: Yes (zero-overhead scheduler, RadixAttention). H100 Qwen3.8-27B 8-bit: 1,725 tok/s at 50 conc vs vLLM 1,610 (Winder.ai 2026-09-25). Llama 3.1 8B at 50 conc: ~3,617 vs vLLM 3,688 (parity).
engines.prefix_caching: RadixAttention automatic prefix cache (default on); best for shared-prefix workloads (e.g. a fixed instruction/system prompt + few-shot in front of each transcript). For unique 3K transcripts only the instruction prefix is reusable.
engines.structured_output: xgrammar (default; JSON schema, regex, EBNF), outlines (JSON, regex), llguidance (all). Works in OpenAI API, native API and offline Engine. SqueezeBits (H100, Qwen3-8B/32B, 2025-09): SGLang stayed closer to unconstrained baseline than vLLM v0.10.0 when guided decoding at batch >= 8 (older versions; re-test).
engines.quantization: FP8, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ (via gptq_marlin), NVFP4 (NVIDIA), ModelOpt FP8/FP4 on Hopper+, GGUF not a focus (UNVERIFIED).
engines.lora: Multi-LoRA (S-LoRA/Punica style), --lora-paths, --max-loras-per-batch (default 8), csgmv backend, dynamic load/unload, pinning, overlap loading. v0.5.23 notes: LoRA now works on quantized MoE models through a new opt-in engine (so MoE-LoRA was a gap until very recently).
engines.hardware: NVIDIA Ampere/Ada/Hopper/Blackwell, AMD, TPU (TorchTPU in 0.5.23), Ascend. Exact SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) status UNVERIFIED; Blackwell B200/GB200 documented on NVIDIA cards.
engines.offline_batch: Yes: sglang.Engine offline engine (python); also OpenAI Batch-style not verified.
engines.cold_start: Comparable to vLLM (<~90 s on 70B FP8 per Spheron); UNKNOWN per target model.
engines.ops_ease: pip/docker (lmsysorg/sglang); more manual flags for hybrid/MoE models; docs lag (supported-models page fetched 2026-11-09 did not list Gemma 4/NemotronH although repo PRs from 2026-11-06..09 show active Gemma4 and NemotronH fixes).
engines.production_readiness: High (xAI, many labs per project claims, not verified); slightly less turnkey than vLLM for odd architectures.
engines.security: No auth by default; same exposure caveats as any HTTP server.
vendor_recommended_by: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4/BF16 cards list SGLang (B200 focus)

engines.continuous_batching: Yes (--parallel slots, continuous batching, unified KV). But scales poorly vs vLLM: Red Hat H200 Llama3.1-8B F16, 64 users: vLLM 44x tokens/s; llama.cpp P99 TTFT >3 min. Winder.ai H100 Qwen3.8-27B: llama.cpp 138 tok/s @10 conc, 97 @50.
engines.prefix_caching: Prompt/slot cache reuse (per-slot, --cache-reuse); less general than vLLM/SGLang.
engines.structured_output: JSON schema -> GBNF grammar conversion; llguidance integration available as build option (UNVERIFIED this session); GBNF native.
engines.quantization: GGUF K-quants/IQ, Q4_K_M etc; new OCP FP8 E4M3 type (v0.9.0); NVFP4 CUDA kernels in active PRs (Nov 2026); MXFP4 (gpt-oss).
engines.lora: GGUF LoRA adapters with hot-swap (--lora, /lora-adapters); merge-and-convert is the usual path.
engines.hardware: CUDA (incl. Ampere/Ada/Hopper/Blackwell), Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, CPU, etc. Single-process; multi-GPU via layer/tensor split; ggml 0.29 adds NCCL multi-node TP.
engines.tensor_parallelism: Limited (split-mode layer/row; new tensor mode in recent builds)
engines.offline_batch: llama-batched / llama-cli, or llama-server with -np; no first-class JSONL batch runner equivalent to run-batch.
engines.ops_ease: Single binary, simplest on odd hardware; requires GGUF conversion; hybrid/SSM kernel perf lags CUDA-first engines.
engines.production_readiness: Good for single-user/low concurrency, edge; not recommended for high-concurrency batch on datacenter GPUs.
engines.security: Bind --host 127.0.0.1 by default for server (verify), --api-key and TLS supported.
vendor_recommended_by: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (GGUF Q4_K_M on RTX 5090)
Google Gemma 4 (day-0 GGUF via HF blog)

engines.maintainers_activity: Very high; company-backed; has its own engine (Go) beyond llama.cpp.
engines.continuous_batching: Weak. OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL default 1 (docs); requests queue. v0.40.15 notes: recurrent and vision GGUF models can now handle multiple simultaneous requests. Red Hat A100-40GB: vLLM peak 793 TPS vs Ollama 41 TPS (Ollama tuned to 32 parallel plateaued). Winder.ai H100 Qwen3.8-27B: 33 tok/s flat at 1/10/50 conc, TTFT 381 s @50.
engines.prefix_caching: Basic prompt cache reuse; UNVERIFIED depth.
engines.structured_output: `format` JSON schema param and OpenAI response_format; implementation not documented in docs (grammar-based underneath per upstream, UNVERIFIED). Ollama cloud does not support it.
engines.quantization: GGUF (Q4_K_M etc.), some MLX; FP8/AWQ/GPTQ not applicable.
engines.lora: Modelfile ADAPTER directive (static per-model); no multi-LoRA batching.
engines.hardware: NVIDIA (CUDA), AMD, Apple, CPU. Works on L4/A100/H100/RTX PRO 6000 in principle.
engines.tensor_parallelism: No true TP (layer split across GPUs).
engines.cold_start: Models stay loaded 5 min by default (OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE). Load time UNKNOWN.
engines.ops_ease: Easiest setup; one command; model library incl. gemma4 (12B/26B/31B/E4B), nemotron-3.5-lightning (19-25GB), granite4.2 (3b 2.2GB, 8b 5.3GB, 30b 18GB).
engines.production_readiness: Dev/prototyping and low-concurrency; not for high-throughput batch.
engines.security: Binds 127.0.0.1:11434 by default (docs), but no authentication; many users expose via OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0. CVE-2026-7482 'Bleeding Llama' (unauthenticated heap OOB read in GGUF loader, disclosed 2026-05-05, ~300k exposed servers reported by Cyera/NYU summary), CVE-2026-5757 (unauthenticated info disclosure in quantization engine, 2026-06-26). Docs state prompts are not sent to external servers locally; cloud models are a separate path.
vendor_recommended_by: NVIDIA developer page lists Ollama for Nemotron
